Description.value: Google Gemini CLI is an open-source, terminal-based AI coding agent developed by Google that brings Gemini model capabilities directly to the developer's command-line environment, supporting multi-turn conversations, file editing, code generation, and agentic web search in a REPL-style interface.

evidence.quote: An open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into your terminal.

Lines_of_Code.value: ~92,242 KB repo size (TypeScript-dominant); estimated 250K+ LOC across packages/cli, packages/core, packages/a2a-server, packages/test-utils, packages/vscode-ide-companion

Contributors.value: 1,000+ (1095 entries returned via paginated GitHub contributors API including anonymous)

Update_Frequency.value: Very high — 10 releases in 14 days (April 12–25, 2026), averaging ~5 releases per week, including nightly preview tags published by gemini-cli-robot.

Practices.Summary: Gemini CLI engineers run a layered test suite with Vitest for unit tests; all contributors must run 'npm run preflight' before PRs which ensures all checks pass by running all tests, linting, and other style checks.

evidence.quote: Ensure all checks pass by running `npm run preflight`. This command runs all tests, linting, and other style checks.

Practices.Summary: Integration tests cover multiple sandbox modes (none, Docker, Podman) to validate shell command execution; developers must run 'npm run test' for unit tests and 'npm run test:e2e' for end-to-end integration tests before submitting changes.

evidence.quote: npm run test for unit tests
npm run test:e2e for integration tests

Practices.Summary: Preflight command acts as comprehensive quality gate that builds the repository, runs all tests, checks for type errors, and lints the code in a single execution to catch issues before CI runs.

evidence.quote: This single command will build the repository, run all tests, check for type errors, and lint the code.

Tools.Summary: Vitest as the unit-test runner; integration test harness with Docker/Podman sandboxes; ESLint and Prettier enforced by preflight; TypeScript type-checking; bundled scripts under scripts/ for build verification.

evidence.quote: This single command will build the repository, run all tests, check for type errors, and lint the code.

Stakeholders.Summary: Core Gemini CLI maintainers at Google (google-gemini org) plus the broader open-source contributor community submitting PRs that must pass preflight in CI.

Practices.Summary: Releases are automated by an in-repo GitHub Actions pipeline driven by the gemini-cli-robot bot, which cuts preview, nightly, and patch releases (e.g., v0.40.0-preview.x) and publishes a gemini-cli-bundle.zip asset per tag. Patch releases are produced by cherry-picking individual commits onto a release/v0.x.y branch and re-tagging. Maintainers review the release PRs created by the bot and Gemini-code-assist bot adds summary od changes

evidence.quote: fix(patch): cherry-pick 048bf6e to release/v0.40.0-preview.3-pr-25941 to patch version v0.40.0-preview.3 and create version 0.40.0-preview.4 by @gemini-cli-robot

Tools.Summary: GitHub Actions workflows under .github/workflows; gemini-cli-robot service account for tagging and asset uploads; npm publish for the @google/gemini-cli package; bundled zip asset distribution from GitHub Releases.

Stakeholders.Summary: Release engineers at Google operating the gemini-cli-robot account; maintainers approving cherry-picks into release branches.

Practices.Summary: Contributors submit small, atomic PRs that address single issues following Google's small CL philosophy; Gemini CLI applies Gemini itself to inspect code diffs through '/review slash command and scripts/review.sh' for AI-assisted preliminary code review.

Practices.Summary: All contributions require signing a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) before code can be merged; PRs must pass preflight checks (tests, linting, type errors) before human review begins.

evidence.quote: Contributions to this project must be accompanied by a Contributor License Agreement
Ensure all checks pass by running `npm run preflight`. This command runs all tests, linting, and other style checks.

Practices.Summary: Google's code review standard emphasizes progressive improvement where reviewers 'approve changes that improve overall code health' rather than demanding perfection; reviews use 'Nit:' prefix for non-blocking suggestions to distinguish required changes from educational comments.

evidence.quote: Reviewers should approve changes that improve the overall code health of the system being worked on, even if the changes aren't perfect.
Use prefix like 'Nit:' to let the author know that it's just a point of polish that they could choose to ignore.

Practices.Summary: Code reviews target one business day maximum response time to maintain development velocity; reviewers aim for 'LGTM with comments' to enable timezone-distributed teams to make progress without blocking on follow-up rounds.

evidence.quote: A reviewer should respond quickly with their review comments. The maximum time it should take to respond to a code review is one business day (the next day).

Tools.Summary: scripts/review.sh (AI-assisted review using Gemini), /review and /review-frontend custom slash commands, GitHub PR review UI, branch protection on main.

Stakeholders.Summary: google-gemini maintainers as code owners; external contributors as PR authors; gemini-cli-robot for automated checks.

Issues.Issue_Title: Plan Mode silently halts execution in YOLO / non-interactive mode waiting for approval
Issues.Description: Agent plan mode stops execution unexpectedly in non-interactive YOLO mode, blocking automated workflows that require approval prompts to be skipped

Issues.Issue_Title: Model steering fails to fallback to Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite when Gemini 3 Flash is exhausted
Issues.Description: Model selection logic does not properly fallback to lower-tier models when primary model quota is exhausted, causing request failures instead of graceful degradation

Issues.Issue_Title: UI Hang when pasting large amounts of text (e.g. 5kiB)
Issues.Description: Terminal interface freezes when users paste large text blocks (>5KB), indicating input buffer or rendering performance issue in the CLI frontend

Issues.Issue_Title: Gemini CLI fails to keep Android Emulator alive despite is_background: true
Issues.Description: Background process management fails to maintain long-running Android Emulator despite is_background flag set to true, causing emulator to terminate prematurely

Issues.Issue_Title: MCP servers remain 'Disconnected' on Windows/WSL despite valid JSON-RPC responses via stdio/HTTP
Issues.Description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server connection detection fails on Windows/WSL even when servers return valid JSON-RPC responses, suggesting platform-specific stdio handling bug

Issues.Issue_Title: Gemini cli bot marks issue as stale and closes it in the same minute
Issues.Description: Stale-bot automation workflow has timing bug that marks and closes issues within same minute without proper grace period, affecting issue lifecycle management

Issues.Issue_Title: Regression: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS in .gemini/.env is ignored since v0.39.0 (PR #24667)
Issues.Description: Environment variable NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS no longer respected after v0.39.0, breaking custom certificate authority configuration for enterprise proxy environments

Issues.Issue_Title: cli breaks on certain prompts which contain code logs
Issues.Description: Parser fails when processing prompts containing structured code logs, indicating regex or parsing vulnerability with specific log formatting patterns

Issues.Issue_Title: bug: MCP tool call hallucination with hyphenated server names
Issues.Description: LLM hallucinates incorrect MCP tool invocations when server names contain hyphens, revealing tokenization or prompt engineering issue in tool name resolution

Issues.Issue_Title: Windows: Regression - run_shell_command strips double quotes
Issues.Description: Shell command execution on Windows incorrectly strips double quotes from arguments after recent changes, breaking commands that require quoted parameters

Practices.Summary: From the 10 issues analyzed, common engineering pitfalls include: (1) platform-specific regressions (Windows/WSL MCP connection, Windows quote stripping), (2) model fallback and quota handling failures, (3) parsing vulnerabilities with edge-case inputs (large text paste, code logs, hyphenated names), (4) background process lifecycle management, and (5) automation timing bugs in bot workflows. The team uses bot-driven triage with /assign and /unassign commands allowing contributors to self-assign up to 3 issues concurrently.

Tools.Summary: GitHub Issues with custom comment-trigger bot, 'help wanted' / 'good first issue' labels, stale-bot, issue templates under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and a triage rotation among maintainers.

Stakeholders.Summary: Issue triagers from the google-gemini team; community contributors who self-assign; the gemini-cli-robot bot.
